newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to March 20.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to March 20.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of March 20 were $10.858 billion, compared to $10.783 billion on March 14.
The central bank said its net international reserves as of March 20 were $20.252 billion, compared to $20.176 billion as of March 14.
The central bank said the increase of $75 million in net international assets in the same time period was due to:
-- Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $245 million.
-- Net sales of $220 million to the federal government to service the foreign debt.

-- A net gain of $50 million dollars for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that between March 14 and March 20 the monetary base rose by 1.919 billion pesos due to an increase in the seasonal demand of bills and coins.
In the same period, net deposits of the federal government in the central bank rose by 2.67 billion pesos as a result of tax collection minus government expenses.
Government securities from Banco de Mexico were reduced by 1.179 billion pesos, chiefly because of maturing government development bonds, known as Bondes.

Banco de Mexico compensated for the reduction of liquidity resulting from the various operations of the federal government, including the maturing Bondes, through a reduction of deposits received from banks by a total of 6.351 billion pesos.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $20.176 bln $20.252 bln
Monetary Base 76.958 78.877
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $10.783 bln $10.858 bln
Net Domestic Credit -9.078 -7.342
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
((--Dan Trotta, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9507))
